subject: Nexa on-prem VPC: thermal isolation, egress acceptance and cutover sync
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nexatherapeutics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nexa NetOps <netops@nexatherapeutics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nexa on-prem: thermal isolation & egress acceptance for upcoming cutover

Hi Rachel,

Following up from last week's call — Nexa is finalizing the on-prem environment at our Fremont colo and we have two immediate asks where we need Redwood's sign-off before we schedule the cutover window:

1) Thermal / rack power isolation: the deployment will be a dense 2U inference cluster in Rack A12. The colo has raised concerns about sustained thermal profiles during sustained 95th-percentile token throughput. I've attached the "nexa-thermal-schematic.pdf" with measured inlet/outlet deltas from our bench runs. We need Redwood's guidance on acceptable thermal headroom and any mechanical/backpressure mitigations the runtime may require.

2) Egress & control/data-plane acceptance: Nexa's security team requires a documented acceptance matrix for any outbound flows from the data plane and the control plane. Specifically: allowed egress destinations, NAT model (customer NAT vs. Redwood egress relay), TLS termination expectations, and observability evidence we'll provide during acceptance.

Proposed timeline: aim for a cutover tentatively during the week of Aug 14. Can Redwood review the attached schematic and provide written acceptance criteria and a short mutual action plan we can include in our change control?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex Morgan
Director, Infrastructure
Nexa Therapeutics
alex.morgan@nexatherapeutics.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: nexa-thermal-schematic.pdf (diagram)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nexatherapeutics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nexa on-prem: thermal isolation & egress acceptance for upcoming cutover

Alex — thanks for the schematic and the clear asks. We've reviewed the file and below are our initial notes and requested evidence to finalize acceptance. I'll loop in engineering for a short technical readout.

High-level recommendations (control/data split):
- Control plane: recommend customer-managed NAT with a restricted outbound ACL to the Redwood control endpoints (control.redwood.ai:443). This keeps telemetry on an authenticated channel and avoids double-NAT complexity.
- Data plane: we support two options; (A) customer NAT egress for token-level calls (preferred for compliance), or (B) Redwood egress-relay for constrained networks (requires additional SLA and routing rules).

Thermal / hardware notes:
- Runtime will throttle worker density if inlet temperatures exceed the per-host threshold (recommended 28C sustained). For initial sign-off we need your rack power profile (per-host max sustained power, inlet temp traces for ≥2 hours at target load).
- If you expect frequent sustained 95th-percentile traffic, we recommend increasing CRAC cycles or reducing node density to one node per 42U block initially.

Acceptance evidence we need from Nexa before cutover:
1) 2-hour thermal run CSV (inlet/outlet, fan speeds) — we can accept the attached CSV format.
2) Network ACL export showing allowed egress FQDNs/IPs and whether NAT is customer-managed.
3) A signed mutual action plan (I attached a short template "mutual-action-plan.md" you can edit).

Next steps:
- Kimberly and Grace: can you confirm the egress-acceptance checklist items (I attached an annotated schematic in the thread once I add notes)?
- Alex: if you can share the 2-hour thermal run and the ACL export by EOD Wed (7/31) we'll queue the SRE canary and set a tentative Aug 14 cutover.

I'll attach a short annotated schematic after internal review.

Best,

Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.md (template)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Nexa on-prem: thermal isolation & egress acceptance for upcoming cutover

Quick technical additions from infra/RUN team:

On Mon, Jul 30, 2028 at 09:12 AM Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nexatherapeutics.com> wrote:
> Following up from last week's call — Nexa is finalizing the on-prem environment at our Fremont colo and we have two immediate asks where we need Redwood's sign-off before we schedule the cutover window:
>
> 1) Thermal / rack power isolation: the deployment will be a dense 2U inference cluster in Rack A12. The colo has raised concerns about sustained thermal profiles during sustained 95th-percentile token throughput.

Notes:
- For control plane keep-alives we will use an mTLS-authenticated outbound connection on 443. No inbound ports required. This means minimal steady-state bandwidth (order of 5–20 kbps per control connection).
- Data-plane egress: if you choose customer NAT, ensure mapping persistence (TCP/UDP timeouts) for long-running streaming responses. If you choose Redwood relay mode, we'll provide a lightweight sidecar that performs TLS passthrough — observable via our tracing headers.
- Canary routing: propose a 3-node canary (1% traffic) with KV-cache warmup off-host to measure thermal delta under real traffic. If temps rise >2.5C over baseline or CPU sustained >85% for >10m, we abort.

Suggested acceptance checklist (quick):
- [ ] 2-hour thermal CSV (inlet/outlet)
- [ ] ACL export + NAT model confirmation
- [ ] Rack PDU logs for host power draw
- [ ] Canary schedule + rollback plan

I'll attach an egress checklist spreadsheet (egress-acceptance-checklist.xlsx) with fields we need for sign-off.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE — Serving Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: egress-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (form)
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nexatherapeutics.com>

Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nexa on-prem: thermal isolation & egress acceptance for upcoming cutover

Rachel / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We ran the 2-hour thermal soak overnight and attached "nexa-thermal-test-results.csv" (sampled 30s). Summary: inlet temps peaked at 26.8C, delta-to-outlet 7.2C, average sustained power per host 395W. PDU logs attached as well.

We prefer customer NAT for egress; ACL export included. We've filled the egress checklist and attached it. We've also edited the mutual-action-plan.md and uploaded the signed copy to DocuSign (link below) — ready to sign on Redwood's side.

Requested next step: please confirm the canary schedule. Our ops window is Aug 14–16 (nightly 00:00–04:00 PDT). If Redwood can accept the window, we'll finalize the change control.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/ABC123-mutual-action-plan
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NEXA-DEPLOY
